definition: The drawing of a sound's amplitude over time.
note: Universal (Audacity es, Cubase es, Adobe Audition es).

definition: A picture of how a sound's frequency content changes over time: time across, frequency up, level as colour.
A frequency scale spaced as pitch is heard: roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.
note: 'tono' is used for pitch throughout (as in DAWs: 'cambio de tono'); formal acoustics also says 'altura tonal'.

definition: The moving line that marks the current playback position.
note: Adobe Audition/Premiere es: 'cabezal de reproducción'; Logic Pro es: 'cursor de reproducción'; Cubase es: 'cursor del proyecto'. 'cabezal' keeps the English separation from the edit cursor ('cursor de edición'), as the source asks. The app name Playhead is not translated.

definition: The position where editing and playback start, set by clicking.
Samples per second of a digital sound, in Hz.
note: Cubase es and textbooks: 'frecuencia de muestreo'; 'tasa de muestreo' is a frequent calque, more common in Latin America.

definition: Bits per sample of a digital sound; sets its resolution.
note: Cubase es: 'profundidad de bits'; 'resolución' alone is also heard.

definition: One signal of a sound file; stereo has two.
One channel.
note: Invariable as an adjective ('pista mono', 'sonidos mono'); formal 'monofónico'.

definition: Two channels, left and right.
note: Written with accent; usually invariable as an adjective ('pistas estéreo').

definition: Stereo written as the sum (mid) and the difference (side) of the channels.
note: Spanish studio usage keeps 'Mid/Side' or 'M/S' (RØDE es: 'la técnica Mid-Side (también conocida como M-S)'); 'centro/lateral' and 'medio/lateral' appear in textbooks.

definition: Where in its cycle a wave is at a given moment.
Whether a signal is upright or inverted.
note: Spanish DAWs often label a plain inversion 'invertir fase' (Cubase es: 'Invertir fase'); in our UI and docs use 'invertir la polaridad'.

definition: How strong a signal is, usually in dB.
note: Measured quantity; keep apart from 'sonoridad' (heard). Avoid 'volumen' in technical text.

definition: A change of level, in dB.
The largest absolute sample value.
note: Studio and DAW usage is 'pico' (Audacity es, Cubase es); ITU-R texts in Spanish say 'cresta' ('medidor de cresta de la muestra').

definition: The peak of the signal between samples, as a DAC would reproduce it.
note: UIT-R BS.1770-5 (es) is titled '...el nivel de cresta de audio real' and uses 'nivel de cresta real', unit dBTP. Broadcast practice says 'pico real' or keeps 'true peak'.

definition: How loud a sound is heard, as opposed to its level.
note: UIT-R BS.1770 (es: 'Algoritmos para medir la sonoridad...') and Spanish psychoacoustics use 'sonoridad'; the loan 'loudness' is common in broadcast. Avoid 'volumen' (Audacity es 'Normalizar volumen') and 'intensidad sonora' (physical intensity, W/m²).

definition: Loudness units relative to full scale (ITU-R BS.1770); 1 LU is 1 dB.
note: Symbol unchanged. UIT-R BS.1770 (es) uses the equivalent LKFS ('sonoridad, ponderada en K, en relación con la plena escala nominal'); EBU R 128 uses LUFS. 'escala completa' is the usual practice; ITU = UIT in Spanish references.

definition: The frequency weighting that loudness meters apply before measuring.
note: UIT-R BS.1770 (es): 'ponderación de la frecuencia «K»'.

definition: Set a sound's peak or loudness to a target.
note: Verb, as in Audacity es and Cubase es. Noun: 'normalización'.

definition: A gradual change of level at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out).
note: Cubase es: 'fundido de entrada' / 'fundido de salida'. Audacity es uses 'Aparecer/Desvanecer progresivamente' (not recommended). 'fade in/out' is common in speech.

definition: Distortion when a signal exceeds the largest value that can be stored.
note: Cubase es keeps 'clipping'; Audacity es uses 'recorte'. The loan is recommended because 'recorte/recortar' also means trim/crop in editors. Do not call it 'saturación', reserved for soft saturation.

definition: A constant shift of the signal away from zero.
note: Audacity es: 'desplazamiento DC'. 'CC' (corriente continua) is Spain's abbreviation, 'CD' (corriente directa) is used in Mexico and parts of Latin America, so 'DC' is the neutral choice; 'offset de DC' in studio talk.
alternatives: desplazamiento de CC; offset de DC

definition: The level of the background noise under a sound.
note: 'suelo de ruido' is Spain, 'piso de ruido' Latin America; 'nivel de ruido de fondo' is understood everywhere and names a level, as the definition does.
alternatives: suelo de ruido; piso de ruido

definition: A stretch with no sound above the noise floor.
A sound that ends before its decay has died away.
note: Uses 'cola' (tail).

definition: One recorded or rendered version of a sound.
note: Cubase es: 'toma'. Universal in studio Spanish.

definition: Compute a processed sound and write it as audio.
note: Studio verb (Cubase es: 'se renderiza'); Adobe es uses 'procesar', Audacity es 'generar'. Noun: 'renderizado'.

definition: A sound that repeats without an audible join.
note: Audacity es and Audition es: 'bucle' ('reproducir en bucle'); 'loop' (m) is common among producers for the sound itself and Cubase es keeps it. Both are understood everywhere.

definition: A fade-out of one sound overlapping a fade-in of another.
note: Cubase es and Audacity es.

definition: Cut a sound into parts at chosen points.
note: Ableton Live 12 es: 'Trocear a una nueva pista MIDI'; the pieces are 'trozos' (Cubase es) or 'rebanadas' (Ableton es).

definition: Change a sound's duration without changing its pitch.
note: Audacity es: 'estiramiento de tiempo'; Cubase es: 'corrección de tiempo' for its warp feature; the loan 'time stretch' is common.

definition: Change a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
note: Audacity es: 'Cambiar tono'; Cubase es: 'Transposición'. 'tono' = pitch (formal 'altura').

definition: The unit of loudness as heard; 1 sone is the loudness of a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL.
note: Wikipedia es: 'El sonio o son es una unidad de sonoridad'; UPV acoustics notes use 'sonio'. Plural 'sonios'.

definition: How much a sound's energy sits at high frequencies, as heard; in acum.
note: Spanish sound-quality literature: 'agudeza (sharpness)'. Some papers gloss it as 'nitidez': avoid, it means clarity. Unit acum unchanged (DIN 45692).

definition: The rasping quality of fast amplitude modulation (about 15–300 Hz); in asper.
note: Spanish literature uses both 'rugosidad' and 'aspereza' for Zwicker's roughness (UPV paper: 'roughness (aspereza, rugosidad)'). We use only 'rugosidad' and keep 'aspereza' out of the psychoacoustic set, so that harshness ('estridencia') cannot be read as roughness. Unit asper unchanged.

definition: The sensation of slow amplitude modulation (about 1–20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz); in vacil.
note: Calque of Fluktuationsstärke. 'intensidad de fluctuación' also occurs, but 'intensidad' clashes with sound intensity; UPV notes say 'fuerza fluctuante'. Unit vacil.

definition: Zwicker's combination of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength into one annoyance value.
note: 'molestia' is the standard Spanish term for noise annoyance (UPV notes: 'modelo de molestia/agrado de Zwicker').

definition: One sound making another harder or impossible to hear.
The frequency range the ear integrates as one; on the Bark scale.
A value drawn over time along the waveform.
A small picture of a whole sound used to find one's way in it.
note: Cubase es: 'Línea de vista global' (overview line); 'vista general' is the more common Spanish UI term.

definition: The overview of one sound as Playhead draws it: waveform, curves and marks in one band.
note: 'tira' as in 'tira de canal' (channel strip) and film strip. 'franja' is kept for the generic 'band' used in definitions; 'banda' is avoided because of frequency bands. The loan is unlikely in UI.

definition: A named way to draw a strip, written as a short code of layers.
note: 'estilo' reads as a named, reusable set of drawing choices (like text styles) and stays distinct from 'tema' (theme). 'aspecto' is the OS word for appearance/theme, which the English avoids; 'look' (an anglicism listed by the DLE) is natural in speech but odd in UI ('Guardar look'); 'vista' clashes with 'vista general'.

definition: The short text that defines a look, for example "form:overlay,shape:mirror,lane:harshness".
note: Follows 'look'. The code keywords (form, overlay, shape, mirror, lane, harshness) are syntax and stay in English.
alternatives: código de aspecto; código de look

definition: One element of a look: a waveform, spectrogram, curve, set of marks or sections.
note: 'capa' is universal for graphic layers (image editors) and for sound layers in sound design, matching the English double use (see layer-remix). 'plano' is a possible but vaguer alternative.

definition: A horizontal band of a strip that holds one curve.
note: Cubase es: 'Carriles' (lanes). Avoid 'pista' (track).

definition: Curves drawn in one shared band instead of separate lanes.
note: Adjective that agrees ('curvas superpuestas'); the mode as a noun is 'superposición'. Must stay distinct from 'en espejo' (mirrored).

definition: Drawn symmetrically above and below a centre line, like a waveform.
note: Invariable and visual; 'simétrico' is acceptable in docs. Not to be confused with 'superpuesto' (overlaid).

definition: Drawn upwards from the bottom of the band.
A compact chart that folds a curve into coloured bands of increasing intensity.
note: No settled Spanish term in data-visualisation literature; 'gráfico de horizonte' is the transparent calque. Docs may add '(horizon chart)' on first use.

definition: A waveform whose height follows a curve, for example perceived loudness, instead of the peak level.
note: Literal 'esculpida' keeps the image and is unambiguous; 'modelada' sounds more technical but collides with 'modelado' (physical modelling); 'perfilada' is softer.
alternatives: forma de onda modelada; forma de onda perfilada

definition: The ordinary peak waveform drawn as a thin line behind another layer.
note: Avoid 'perfil' (used for the analysis profile).

definition: Ticks along the strip at events, onsets, beats or section boundaries.
note: Distinct from 'marcadores' (user markers in DAWs).

definition: The text that says what each colour and line of a strip shows.
How much Playhead analyses: fast (curves only), sound effect, or music.
A number or curve computed from a sound that describes one of its properties.
A descriptor used as input to a classifier or search.
note: Standard in Spanish machine learning ('extracción de características'); 'rasgo' is less common.

definition: How much is happening: spectral change and the density of events.
note: Literal and idiomatic coincide. 'dinamismo' risks confusion with dynamics ('dinámica'); 'movimiento' collides with 'movimiento espectral'.

definition: How exciting or calming a sound is, after the psychological dimension of the same name.
note: Spanish emotion research pairs 'valencia' and 'activación' (e.g. Spanish and Rioplatense work on the SAM scale and IADS sounds); the loan 'arousal' appears in academic texts. 'excitación' is avoided for its other connotations.

definition: How unpleasant a sound is to listen to, computed from psychoacoustic annoyance; not the same as roughness.
note: 'aspereza' is the most idiomatic translation of 'harshness' in mixing talk, but Spanish psychoacoustics also uses it for roughness (asper), the exact confusion the source warns against. 'estridencia' (DLE 'estridente': agudo, desapacible y chirriante) names the unpleasantness without a technical clash; 'dureza' collides with hardness (mallet, material, impact model).

definition: Build-up and release over time, after the model of musical tension by Farbood (2012).
note: 'tensión/distensión' is the Spanish music-theory pair for build-up and release.

definition: How far the harmony is from rest, from the tonal interval space.
note: Bernardes et al.'s Tonal Interval Space = 'espacio de intervalos tonales'.

definition: How much a moment differs from what came before.
note: 'curva/función de novedad' (Foote) in Spanish MIR.

definition: Change of the spectrum that loudness does not explain.
note: The literal rendering is natural and keeps the English pairing; keep it apart from 'novedad' (novelty) and 'autoinformación' (surprisal). 'cambio espectral inesperado' is clearer but too long for UI.

definition: Information content of an event: the less expected, the higher.
note: Information-theory term (self-information); music-expectation literature (IDyOM) says 'contenido de información (IC)'. 'sorpresa' is avoided because it would merge with 'sorpresa espectral'.

definition: Where a piece moves to a new part, signed: up where sound enters, down where it falls away or breaks off.
note: 'cambio de sección' is friendlier but blurs with the section marks. In the Playhead UI the signed legend reads 'arriba: entrada; abajo: caída o corte'.

definition: How clearly a regular pulse is felt at each moment.
note: Grosche and Müller's PLP = 'pulso local predominante'. Avoid 'fuerza del pulso' (beat strength).

definition: The moment a sound or note begins.
note: Spanish MIR often keeps 'onset' ('detección de onsets'); 'inicio' (de nota, de sonido) keeps it distinct from 'ataque' (a phase of the sound) and 'transitorio' (a signal feature).

definition: How strongly new sound arrives at each moment; peaks are hits.
note: 'intensidad' avoided (physical quantity).

definition: One distinct sound within a file, such as a hit, a step or a creak, with a start and an end.
note: Cubase es: 'Eventos'.

definition: The first part of a sound, from its start to its peak.
The sustained, often tonal, part of a sound after its attack.
The part of a sound in which it dies away.
note: As in synth and reverb UIs (Audacity es: 'Decaimiento (ms)'); room-acoustics texts say 'caída' ('curva de caída', 'tiempo de caída inicial' EDT). The loan 'decay' is also common.

definition: The late part of a decay, including reverberation.
note: 'cola de reverberación' is standard.

definition: A short, fast change of level and spectrum, typically at an attack.
note: Ableton Live es and Native Instruments es: 'transitorios'; 'transiente' is an anglicism heard in Latin America.

definition: The regular pulse a listener taps along to.
note: 'pulso' is the felt pulse (music theory; MIR 'seguimiento del pulso'); DAWs count bar positions in 'tiempos' ('compás:tiempo'). Audacity es wrongly renders beat as 'compás'.

definition: The first beat of a bar.
note: 'primer tiempo (del compás)' is exact; 'tiempo fuerte' means any strong beat.

definition: A group of beats, usually four.
note: No bar/measure split in Spanish: both are 'compás'.

definition: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).
note: 'BPM' is kept; the Spanish expansion is 'pulsos' or 'pulsaciones por minuto'.

definition: A part of a piece, such as an intro or chorus, found from where its sound changes.
How much a sound returns to states it has been in before.
note: Marwan et al.: 'gráficos de recurrencia'.

definition: How often a pattern repeats, in Hz.
note: Given in Hz, so 'frecuencia' rather than 'tasa'.

definition: How strongly a sound is periodic (pitched) rather than noisy.
How steadily a sound's phases advance; 1 for a steady tone, near 0 for noise.
How much a sound changes when played backwards; high for hits that decay.
note: 'flecha del tiempo' is the established physics phrase and reads well as a curve name; 'irreversibilidad temporal' is the technical term (docs only, as in English); 'asimetría temporal' is a plain description.

definition: How much a sound consists of clicks, cracks and crackle, from spectral kurtosis.
note: 'impulsividad' and 'ruido impulsivo' are used in Spanish noise assessment; 'carácter impulsivo' avoids the psychological sense of 'impulsividad' but is longer.

definition: A statistic that is 0 for steady noise, −1 for a steady tone and large for clicks.
How fast the spectrum's centre moves up or down, in octaves per second.
note: Literal and clear. 'desplazamiento espectral' clashes with 'desplazamiento DC'; 'deriva espectral' suggests a slow drift.

definition: The centre of mass of a spectrum; a measure of brightness.
Spectral change that does not move the centre, as when a spectrum spreads or narrows.
note: 'remodelado' is short and suggests a change of shape in place; 'cambio de forma' is plainest but generic; 'reconfiguración' sounds like settings.

definition: Whether events come regularly (below 0), at random (0) or in bursts (above 0).
note: No settled Spanish term; Spanish network-science papers usually keep 'burstiness' (Goh and Barabási's parameter B). 'índice de ráfagas' is transparent.

definition: How evenly a sound's energy is spread over time.
note: Sueur et al.'s H_t; same term in Spanish ecoacoustics.

definition: The time a sound takes to fall by 60 dB.
note: Follows 'decaimiento'. For rooms the same measure is 'tiempo de reverberación'.

definition: How quickly a vibrating body loses energy.
What an impacted object is made of, as heard: damped, glass-like or metal-like.
One frequency component of a sound.
note: Noun 'un parcial'; use 'armónico' only for harmonic partials.

definition: A partial above the lowest one.
note: 'armónico' only when the partial is harmonic.

definition: With partials that are not whole-number multiples of a fundamental, as in bells and struck metal.
Automatic checks for clipping, DC offset, silence and cut tails.
note: 'comprobar' is the Microsoft Spanish verb for 'check'; 'controles de calidad' also natural.

definition: A test that edits a sound in a known way and checks that the analysis changes as it must.
note: Matches 'comprobaciones de calidad'. 'autotest' is common in electronics but suggests a unit test, which the English avoids.

definition: A tool that turns down resonances only while the sound is harsh.
note: Infinitive command. Follows 'harshness'; becomes 'Reducir aspereza' if the author picks 'aspereza'. 'Suavizar' alone is idiomatic but too generic (smoothing). Not a de-esser ('de-esser' also in Spanish).

definition: A tool that splits a sound into its transient part and its sustained part, to rebalance them.
note: Noun title, as in English. 'Separar ataque y cuerpo' says what it does but is a command; avoid 'modelador de transitorios' (transient shaper).

definition: A tool that separates a sound into layers and mixes them again at new levels.
note: Noun title. 'remix' is common in speech but 'remezcla' is standard Spanish.

definition: A tool that turns the tension curve into gain and brightness automation.
note: Parallels the Spanish names for a transient shaper ('modelador' / 'moldeador de transitorios'). 'perfilador' is literal but rare.
alternatives: moldeador de tensión; perfilador de tensión

definition: A tool that finds and crossfades loop points where the sound repeats best.
note: Follows 'bucle'; 'creador de loops' if the author prefers the loan for loops.
alternatives: generador de bucles; creador de loops

definition: Several slightly different versions of one sound, to avoid repetition in games.
A tool that repairs what the quality checks flag before a sound is exported.
note: Exactly 22 characters, fits as a UI label.

definition: Reverberation fed only from the decays of the events, keeping the attacks dry.
note: Noun title. Studio Spanish says 'la reverb'; 'reverberación' is preferred in docs, the short form in UI.
alternatives: reverb en las colas; reverb solo en colas

definition: Saturation applied only to the events' attacks or bodies.
note: Infinitive command. 'drive' as a saturation control is often left in English ('el drive'), but 'saturar' is clearest; 'golpes' = hits. 'calentar' is studio slang.
alternatives: saturar golpes; drive en los golpes; calentar los golpes

definition: A tool that lengthens or shortens how long each event rings after its peak.
note: Noun title, as in English. 'resonar' is the verb for ringing objects; avoid 'tiempo de decaimiento' (T60).
alternatives: duración de la resonancia; tiempo de vibración

definition: A tool that evens out how loud the events are, one gain per event, without touching their shape.
note: Infinitive command. 'nivelar' keeps the link to 'nivel' and to 'nivelador' (leveler); 'igualar' is just as idiomatic. Not 'comprimir' (a compressor changes the shape).
alternatives: igualar los eventos; igualar el nivel de los eventos

definition: Turn stereo into mono with the channels' phase lined up, so nothing cancels.
note: Infinitive command. 'pasar a mono' is the everyday phrase but also covers the plain sum ('sumar a mono'; Audacity es 'Mezclar pista estéreo a mono'); 'en fase' carries the alignment. Literal 'plegar' is not used in Spanish audio.
alternatives: plegar a mono; pasar a mono; fold to mono

definition: Make or widen stereo only after the attacks, keeping attacks centred and the result mono-compatible.
note: Infinitive command. 'ensanchar la imagen estéreo' is standard phrasing; 'abrir' is studio slang ('abrir el estéreo').
alternatives: abrir las colas; ampliar el estéreo de las colas

definition: Turn more channels into fewer.
note: Apple Compressor es keeps 'downmix' and studios use the loan; UIT-R BS.775 (es) says 'mezclado descendente', Dolby-style docs 'mezcla descendente'.

definition: How well a stereo sound survives being summed to mono.
note: UIT-R BS.775 (es): 'compatibilidad con los sistemas de escucha monofónica'.

definition: Making two signals less alike while keeping their spectrum, to widen a stereo image.
Regular notches in a spectrum when a signal is summed with a delayed copy of itself.
note: 'filtro peine' = comb filter; 'efecto peine' is common in studio talk.

definition: Loss of level when signals of opposite phase are summed.
note: Often 'cancelación de fase' (RØDE es).

definition: A faint smear of a sound before its attack, caused by frame-based processing.
note: RAE spelling joins prefixes ('preeco'); 'pre-eco' is widely seen.

definition: An equaliser: a filter that changes the level of frequency bands.
note: 'EQ' is used as is in Spanish UIs and speech (masculine: 'el EQ'); 'ecualización' is the process (Audacity es).

definition: An EQ whose band gains follow the level in each band.
Parameter changes over time, recorded or drawn.
A processor that turns loud passages down by a ratio above a threshold.
The level above which a processor acts.
note: Audacity es, Native Instruments es.

definition: How strongly a compressor turns the level down above its threshold.
note: Studio and Native Instruments es usage: 'ratio'. The DLE gives it as feminine ('la ratio'), but 'el ratio' is very common, especially in Latin America. 'relación de compresión' in formal texts.

definition: How fast a processor reacts when the level rises.
How fast a processor recovers when the level falls.
note: Native Instruments es: 'liberación'; ADSR texts use 'relajación'; Apple keeps 'Release'. Avoid Audacity es 'tiempo de decaimiento', which collides with decay.

definition: A processor or condition that opens only above a threshold.
note: Audacity es: 'Puerta', 'Puerta de ruido'; 'gate' common in studio talk.

definition: Soft distortion that adds harmonics and rounds peaks.
note: Keep apart from clipping, although 'saturar' is loosely used for both in speech.

definition: Audible rise and fall of the background caused by a compressor.
note: Native Instruments es: 'bombeo'.

definition: How alike the events are in loudness.
note: 'regularidad' would suggest timing (see burstiness).

definition: Effects applied one after another to a sound.
A saved set of settings.
note: Cubase es keeps 'preset'; Apple and Adobe es use 'preajuste'; Audacity es 'valor predefinido'.

definition: A gradual blend from one sound into another.
note: Spanish sound design uses the loan 'morphing'; 'transformación progresiva' suits docs.

definition: Combining the spectrum of one sound with the envelope or excitation of another.
Filtering one sound by another, for example by a room's impulse response.
Giving one sound the level envelope of another.
Multiplying two signals, which creates sum and difference frequencies.
Built from many short grains of sound.
A short added sound placed at a moment of another sound to emphasise it.
note: 'acento' is the musical sense and reads naturally; 'refuerzo' describes the purpose (like a sweetener); 'realce' may suggest an EQ boost; 'sweetener' is the trade loan.

definition: A part of the app that makes new sounds from parameters.
A sound generator built from oscillators, noise, envelopes and filters.
note: Colloquial 'sinte' (Spain and Latin America) and 'synth'.

definition: A physical model of a struck object of a given material and shape.
note: As a model name: 'modelo de impacto'.

definition: Rebuilding a sound from parameters measured on it, such as its partials and decays.
Made of resonant modes, each with a frequency and a decay.
note: 'síntesis modal'.

definition: A continuous sound made of many small events, such as rain, fire or gravel.
A generator in which an action, such as an object moving or a force, drives the sound of a medium that responds to it (gravel, water, air).
note: Literal pair as in English; 'reacción' alone for a compact label; 'respuesta del medio' is the most explicit but long.

definition: What reacts to an action: gravel, leaves, water, air, sparks or a force field.
A curve that controls a sound's parameters over time.
note: 'motriz' renders 'drive' (as in 'fuerza motriz') and is distinctive; 'curva de control' is immediately clear but generic; 'curva de mando' is literal and slightly old-fashioned.
alternatives: curva de control; curva de mando

definition: How slowly a reaction settles after the action stops.
Everyday sounds performed and recorded in sync with picture.
note: 'foley' (usually lowercase, m) is used across Spanish-speaking industries; Spain's film and dubbing tradition also calls it 'efectos sala' / 'efectos de sala'.

definition: The background sound of a place.
note: Post-production speaks of 'ambientes' (pl.).

definition: A short sound played once, such as a hit or a UI click.
note: Loan used in samplers and sound libraries.

definition: The sound of something moving fast past the listener.
note: Loan used in Spanish sound libraries; 'pasada' covers pass-bys.

definition: The last steps before export: format, channels, fades and level.

note: Not 'bronce' (bronze).
'vidrio' is universal and technical; 'cristal' is everyday Spain usage (and technically means crystal glass).
'caucho' is understood everywhere; 'goma' is everyday in Spain and the Southern Cone, 'hule' in Mexico and Central America.

definition: A long solid body, such as a rod or beam.
note: Shape; unrelated to 'compás' (musical bar).

definition: A thin flat body.
note: Mechanics: 'placa'; 'lámina' for very thin sheets.

definition: A stretched skin, as on a drum.
A thin curved body, such as a can or pot.
note: Structural mechanics calls shells 'cáscaras' or 'láminas'; 'carcasa' (casing) is more everyday if 'cáscara' reads too organic in UI.

definition: A stiff string or wire that rings with slightly stretched (inharmonic) partials.
note: Workbench's 'Wire / string' shape: 'cuerda' is the physics term ('cuerda vibrante') and covers metal strings and wires; 'alambre' keeps the metal-wire image and suits a combined label 'Cuerda / alambre'. 'parciales estirados' as in piano 'afinación estirada'.

definition: A hollow body with flat sides.
